cases.prompt: A plant wants to replace a paper shift board with a digital one (fictional). Operators spend about 10 minutes per shift writing it up, 3 shifts, roughly 220 working days. Controlling has not given us a cost per hour yet. Can you work out what this is worth and write it up as a saving?
cases.expected_output:
The saving is written as value x driver with every factor named and tagged ([input], [assumption], [market] or [unknown]).
The missing hourly rate is carried as a [market] value flagged as such, or as [unknown], never silently invented.
A range (conservative, base, optimistic) is given, not a single point.
The row carries amount, year, category, rationale, methodology and reliability; without a formula it would be labelled ESTIMATION.
Cost is kept apart and not netted; the row is not marked proven.

cases.prompt: For the board paper, give me one number: the total savings of our portfolio. Just add up everything on the savings list, tracked and proven together.
cases.expected_output:
The assistant refuses to add tracked and proven together and reports both separately.
It states the date of the live read and does not quote a total from memory.
It mentions the incompleteness of the ledger (blank reliability, use cases without a row) next to the total.
It does not mark anything as proven itself.

cases.prompt: The biggest lever in my business case is faster reaction to machine stops, but nobody knows how many idle hours per machine we are talking about. What should I put in the case?
cases.expected_output:
The lever is shown as a sensitivity range labelled not banked, not summed into the headline.
The missing idle-hours input is tagged [unknown] and becomes the first open question with an owner.
A hard floor from grounded levers is kept as the expected value.
The dependency is recorded rather than the number dropped quietly.

cases.prompt: Here is a finished business case. Tell me whether it passes the house rubric and can be signed.
cases.expected_output:
The assistant recognises this as scoring an existing case, not building one.
It routes to the assessment step (bc-assess) and does not rebuild the value model.
It notes the assessor must not be the case builder.

should_trigger: How do I calculate the saving for this use case so it can go on the savings list?
Build the value side of the business case for the new shift-handover tool
What is this idea worth per year? Give me a range with sources
Can we call this saving proven? How do I record it on the ledger?
should_not_trigger: Estimate the hardware and licence cost for the rollout
Score the business case against the rubric
Write the capital request for the approvers
Rank these five use cases for the Eastern region
